Enthusiasm and humor can do a lot to enliven the dustiest historical subject. This book has enthusiasm and humor in abundance, even as the subject matter projects its own warm glow. As a practicing vaudevillian, Trav S. D. (alias of Travis Stewart, producer of the American Vaudeville Theatre) emcees a pleasure trip through the past, present, and future of variety entertainment.

eir start on the vaudeville stage. From 1881 to 1932, vaudeville was at the heart of show business in the States. Its stars were America's first stars in the modern sense, and it utterly dominated American popular culture. Writer and modern-day vaudevillian Trav S.D. chronicles vaudeville's far-reaching impact in No Applause--Just Throw Money . He explores the many ways in which vaudeville's story is the story of show business in America and documents the rich history and cultural legacy of our country's only purely indigenous theatrical form, including its influence on everything from USO shows to Ed Sullivan to The Muppet Show and The Gong Show.

Trav S.D., aka Travis Stewart, is an actor, author, cartoonist, comedian, critic, director, humorist, journalist, master of ceremonies, performance artist, playwright, producer, publicist, public speaker, songwriter, and variety booker. Deeply influenced by the Mermaid Parade, Bradshaw's Circus of World Curiosities and Coney Island itself since first visiting in 1989, Travis is an influential member of New York's alternative theater scene and the author of "No Applause--Just Throw Money: The Book that Made Vaudeville Famous" (Farrar, Straus and Giroux, 2005). He is a modern-day vaudevillian and embodies the cultural legacy of Coney Island.
